implementation_approach: Implement order cancellation by extending the Order domain model with a status enum field (OrderStatus: 'pending' | 'cancelled') and optional cancellation metadata fields (cancelledAt timestamp). Add a cancelOrder(orderId) API wrapper function in orderApi.ts following the established pattern of existing functions like createOrder and getMyOrders. Implement the core business logic in the mock API client (shared/api/client.ts) by adding a POST /orders/:id/cancel endpoint that validates cancellation eligibility (order must exist, must be in 'pending' status, cannot already be cancelled), then updates the order status in memory. Enhance OrderHistoryPage component to display conditional cancel buttons only for pending orders, add a loading state during cancellation (cancellingId state), and integrate error handling through the existing ApiError pattern. Update the orderStorage layer to persist the cancelled status through existing saveOrder and replaceOrderHistory functions (backward compatible). The implementation follows established architectural patterns: feature-sliced organization, thin API facade pattern, centralized business logic in mock client, React hooks for component state, and existing error infrastructure.
coupling_observations: The implementation introduces moderate coupling at the domain layer: (1) Order model extension (status field) cascades through API responses, storage serialization, and component rendering logic - any model change requires updates across three layers; (2) Mock API client becomes the single point of validation logic for cancellation rules - centralizes logic but creates a larger, more complex client.ts file; (3) OrderHistoryPage tightly couples data fetching, state management, and cancellation UI logic within one component - would benefit from sub-component extraction if cancellation grows to include confirmation modals; (4) Cancellation state must coordinate with existing reviewStatus field to avoid invalid combinations (e.g., cancelled orders should not have active review deadlines); (5) Error handling integrates cleanly with existing ApiError infrastructure - minimal new coupling required; (6) Storage layer maintains backward compatibility through optional fields - cancelled orders gracefully handled by existing persistence logic; (7) No external system dependencies introduced - feature remains self-contained within client-side architecture. The layered architecture naturally contains coupling, but mock client complexity and component state management are the primary concerns for future refactoring.
duplication_observations: Code duplication is well-controlled through existing abstractions: (1) Error handling pattern already established - cancellation errors (404 'order not found', 400 'already cancelled') map to messageForErrorCode function pattern in errorMessages.ts, no new error handling needed; (2) API request pattern established in orderApi.ts with createOrder, getMyOrders, and new functions follow identical auth: true pattern - cancelOrder function requires no new abstractions; (3) Async state management in OrderHistoryPage uses existing useState/try-catch pattern for loading/error states - cancellation reuses existing error state and adds minimal new state (cancellingId for button disabled state); (4) Button component library already exists with disabled state support - no need for new button variants, existing Button component used with disabled={cancellingId === order.id}; (5) Confirmation dialog not yet implemented in first iteration - represents new UI pattern that could be extracted to shared/ui/Modal for future reuse (delete, batch operations); (6) Storage persistence mirrors existing saveOrder pattern in orderStorage.ts - minimal duplication; (7) No duplication of API endpoint pattern - mock client route matching follows established regex pattern. Main opportunity for reduction: if future features require confirmation modals, extract current inline confirmation logic to reusable component.
responsibility_observations: Proper separation of concerns across architectural layers: (1) Order entity model (entities/order/model.ts) responsibility: domain structure definition only - add OrderStatus type and cancelledAt field, no business logic embedded; (2) API wrapper facade (api/orderApi.ts) responsibility: thin client interface - cancelOrder(orderId) function providing typed interface to backend, auth handling delegated to request(); (3) Mock API client (shared/api/client.ts) responsibility: all business validation rules - time window checks (if implemented), status verification, ownership validation, state transitions, error generation; (4) OrderHistoryPage responsibility: presentation and user orchestration - conditional rendering of cancel buttons, loading states during operation, error display, delegates validation to API layer; (5) orderStorage responsibility: persistence only - saveOrder and replaceOrderHistory functions handle cancelled status opaquely, no cancellation-specific logic; (6) Error handling (shared/api/errorMessages.ts) responsibility: error code translation only - messageForErrorCode maps error codes to user-facing messages, no logic; (7) Button/Modal components responsibility: pure presentation - no business logic, consume onClick callbacks. This clean separation enables independent testing of business logic (mock API), UI behavior (component tests), and integration (end-to-end).
changeability_observations: The implementation establishes patterns enabling future order-state evolution: (1) Order model gains status field supporting future state transitions - extensible for future order lifecycle states (confirmed, ready, delivered, returned, refunded) without breaking current implementation; (2) Cancellation timestamp (cancelledAt) optional field supports future audit trail, analytics, and retention policy features - adding required reason field later requires only new optional field, no breaking changes; (3) Business rule centralization in mock API client enables future customization - cancellation window, store-specific policies, order-type restrictions can be parameterized without client changes; (4) Error code pattern extensible - new cancellation-specific error codes integrate naturally with existing messageForErrorCode pattern; (5) Modal extraction opportunity - any future confirmation requirements (delete order, modify, appeal) benefit from shared Modal component; (6) Component conditional rendering scales to other order actions - current if(order.status === 'pending') pattern extends to if(order.status === 'confirmed') for reschedule, if(order.status === 'ready') for pickup confirmation; (7) Mock cancellation endpoint is migration-ready - no client-side changes needed when moving to real backend API, request path and method already match typical REST patterns; (8) Storage layer supports state machine migration - if lifecycle grows complex, current optional status field and backward-compatible persistence support migration to more sophisticated state management; (9) Future complexity: as order states grow beyond pending/cancelled, consider extracting state machine logic to separate module (order-state-machine.ts) with transition validation, preventing invalid state combinations. Current implementation avoids premature abstraction while keeping refactoring path clear.
